messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing a pretty weird interaction between client-side pause (browser tab backgrounding) and our SSE stream handling. When clients pause/resume we sometimes double-count tokens and the connection ends up in a 'parked' state where KV-cache flushes are delayed. Repro + logs below.

kevin: Ugh. Do we have a minimal repro? Is this client or server side?

maria: Minimal repro: open a streaming chat, background the tab for ~10s, then foreground. curl repro: `curl -N -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \"https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/streams/streamId\"` — then hit Ctrl+Z to pause, fg to resume. On the server side we saw: 

```
2026-02-11T15:22:03.123Z stream:conn=abc123 state=streaming tokens=432
2026-02-11T15:22:11.987Z stream:conn=abc123 client=paused
2026-02-11T15:22:21.004Z stream:conn=abc123 client=resumed tokens=210
2026-02-11T15:22:21.010Z billing:conn=abc123 tokens_charged=642  # should not double-charge for paused window
2026-02-11T15:22:21.011Z kvcache:conn=abc123 flush=deferred
```

maria: The billing line is the thing — tokens charged at resume equal the cumulative tokens produced plus tokens that were already counted while paused. Also KV-cache flush is deferred until we fully ACK the resume, which means some downstream writes get delayed.

dinesh: My guess: when we detect a pause (TCP window or write F/E again), we switch the per-connection state to PARKED but keep emitting internal token accounting events. On resume we re-emit the pending partial frames and increment the billed tokens. We never persisted that the last-billed-offset before park should be the base on resume.

sara: Console impact: dashboards show a steady token/s spike at resume and latency percentiles jump because KV flush backlog appears. There's no dedicated metric for pause/resume events so troubleshooting is noisy.

kevin: Sounds like two action buckets: 1) fix accounting so PARKED/resume doesn't double-bill, 2) add telemetry and a short TTL for parked sessions (so they don't hold cache flush forever). Any downsides?

maria: Accounting fix needs to be careful for partial chunks and for function/tool calls (where side-effect idempotency matters). If we treat paused tokens as "in-flight but not billed" we need deterministic semantics for reconnects and for multi-worker handoffs.

dinesh: Implementation idea: add a per-connection offset checkpoint that we persist to redis when we mark PARKED. On resume we reconcile: skip re-billing up to checkpoint. Also add a flag `billing_paused=true` so internal token-emitter doesn't increment cost metrics while parked. That avoids double-charge and keeps metric continuity.

sara: Telemetry: please emit events `stream.pause`, `stream.resume`, `stream.parked_ttl_expired` with tags: conn_id, tenant_id, cause (client_signal|proxy_idle|tcp_rto). Then update Console to show a small heatmap for paused sessions.

kevin: Agree. Also edge-case: mobile SDKs sometimes intentionally pause for network flaps and expect seamless resume. If we TTL park too aggressively we risk disconnects that are surprising. Recommend config: default park_ttl=30s, escalated for enterprise customers up to 5m via tenant config.

maria: For immediate mitigation we can: 1) short-circuit billing increments while we see the client unreadable state, 2) add a one-line dashboard graph for paused sessions to help SRE detect regressions. Both are low-risk.

kevin: Assigning: @dinesh to prototype checkpoint+billing_paused change (PR + unit tests). @maria to add curl repro script to infra-tests and add the KV-flush observation to the integration test harness. @sara to open a telemetry ticket and a small Console card mock.

ops-agent: Created task STREAM-PAUSE-106 in Jira for the combined work: prototype + telemetry + console. Priority P2. Link: https://jira.internal/STREAM-PAUSE-106

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: will roll a canary of the billing_paused flag to staging in 2h, production after tests pass.

maria: I'll post the curl script and the recorded logs to the ticket. Also adding a short note for support templates: how to detect this from customer traces.

kevin: Thanks — let's keep the patch small and gated. If anyone finds additional repros (esp via proxy or mobile SDK), paste them here. :thumbsup:

dinesh: Will start a branch and ping for review in ~45m.

maria: FYI — observed one tenant with high prevalence of this when using our experimental proxy. Might be related to NGINX buffering config; will test.
